To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fit and coating characteristics of the implant can significantly influence the adaptive bone remodeling process.

the amount of bone loss is reduced by using press-fit rather than overreamed stems, by using fully coated rather than noncoated or partly coated stems, and by using partly coated rather than fully coated stems, if the coating is applied only to a small region at proximal part of a press-fit stem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the fit and bonding characteristics between femoral stem implants and bone, on the bone remodeling process.
the effects of fit, bonding and coating characteristics of femoral implants on adaptive bone remodeling, and the long term fixation of uncemented hip stems.
the prediction of bone remodeling around hip implants, with the goal of developing an optimal design of uncemented hip stems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the computer predictions indicate that a proximally coated stem is not necessarily the best solution.
a fully coated stem with a good fit (overreamed) should be preferred to a partly coated or a noncoated stem.
the fit of the stem in the bone and the bonding characteristics of the stem to bone are of major importance in preventing the bone loss around hip stems, especially in the proximal regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a press-fit, fully coated stem, which is not cemented, is the worst design in terms of bone loss.
the fit and bonding characteristics are the most important factors that determine the amount of stress shielding and the resulting adaptive bone remodeling around femoral stems.

, the computer predictions showed that the bone remodeling theory can be used to predict the bone loss around uncemented femoral stems, when the unknown parameters used in the adaptive bone remodeling theory are established (triggered).
The main takeaway from our work is that
a better fit of the stem to the bone, as well as the use of a fully coated surface, is beneficial for the long-term success of uncemented hip stems.

, for the long-term survival of a press-fit stem, it is essential that a good initial fit is achieved, and that the stem should not be overreamed, because this may cause excessive bone atrophy and loosening of the stem.

the bone density distribution around a press-fit stem is less affected by stress shielding than around a fully coated stem, and that a proximally coated stem is less affected than a fully coated stem.
